Title: The Pain That Won't Stop Isn't Bad Luck - Diet Can Shift Your Risk

Description:
About one in ten women of reproductive age has endometriosis — tissue that acts like the uterine lining but grows outside it, on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvic lining. Unlike typical cramps, this pain often continues before and after your period, radiates to your lower back or thighs, and can show up during sex or bowel movements.

A 12-year Harvard study following over 100,000 nurses found trans fat raises risk by 48% (mainly from fried foods eaten outside the home, margarine, and crackers), while women with the highest omega-3 intake were 22% less likely to be diagnosed.

About 40% of women with endometriosis experience infertility, and 25-50% of women being treated for infertility turn out to have the condition.

If your pain lingers past your period or shows up during sex or bowel movements, talk to a gynecologist — cutting back on fried food and adding fatty fish like salmon can support your treatment plan.

Pelvic pain that doesn't stop when your period does? 😖 It might not just be bad luck.

Endometriosis affects about 1 in 10 women of reproductive age. A 12-year Harvard study found trans fat (fried food, margarine, crackers) raised risk by 48%, while omega-3s lowered it by 22%.

If the pain continues after your period or shows up during sex, talk to a gynecologist — and try swapping in more fatty fish like salmon.
